reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared patterns with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations, ensuring both contextual insight and statistical validation. This approach effectively isolates features that are common across instances and have high model attribution despite lacking semantic relevance to the target class.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 36754) and evaluate their semantic relevance to class prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: List of shared features across all three instances, and a preliminary assessment of their semantic plausibility in relation to income prediction

autonomous_tasks.query: Why might a shared feature, such as 'relationship=Husband' or 'marital-status=Married-civ-spouse', be spurious in this context despite being present in all misclassified instances?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Hypothesis on the spurious nature of the shared feature, particularly if it correlates with misclassification due to data leakage or biased training relationships

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides consistent feature attribution across instances, highlighting which features have high influence despite being semantically irrelevant. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability and gradient-based importance to validate spurious patterns. Sensitivity analysis directly tests the impact of removing each feature, confirming whether the misclassification persists when the shared feature is ablated, thus verifying spuriousness.
